question.text: A plane electromagnetic wave is incident on a plane surface of area A, normally and is perfectly reflected. If energy E strikes the surface in time $t$ then force exerted on the surface is ( $c=$ speed of light)

solution.text:
Incident momentum, $p=\frac{E}{c}$

For perfectly reflecting surface with normal incidence

$\Delta p=2 p=\frac{2 \mathrm{E}}{c} ; \mathrm{F}=\frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}=\frac{2 \mathrm{E}}{c t}$
